newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 11.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Friday.

WASHINGTON - The Clinton Administration proposed giving every school and library in the United States free access to the Internet with the cost to be paid collectively by the nation's communications carriers.

WASHINGTON - Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole's advisers always claimed that a reputation for integrity was one of his greatest attributes. Now, many Republicans are wondering why the Dole campaign has failed to make the ethics case against President Bill Clinton.

MURMANSK, Russia - The region around Murmansk contains without doubt the most dangerous concentration of nuclear hazards in the world, including at least 70 idle and deteriorating nuclear-powered submarines.

SUMMERVILLE, South Carolina - Senator Strom Thurmond may be 93, hard of hearing, slow of foot and prone to lose his place when paragraphs get too long, but he delivers the goods for his state in a way most politicians only dream of.

WASHINGTON - Two members of Washington D.C. Mayor Marion Barry's security detail drove voters to polling places in southeast Washington where Barry was campaigning for a council member in last month's primary elections.
WASHINGTON - Thirty days shy of her 106th birthday Henriette Bolane, who was born in Haiti, became an American citizen -- the oldest new American in known history.
